title: Kairos: Toward Adaptive and Parameter-Efficient Time Series Foundation Models
claim: Ours beats larger existing models with far fewer parameters, motivated by uneven information density that fixed tokenization ignores but adaptive tokenization handles.
layout: 4 panels: large scatter-line plot left, bar chart and tokenization diagram middle, time-series column right
description: A four-panel figure. Panel (a), on the left, is a line-and-marker plot of MASE against parameter count on a log axis. Colored series for Moirai, Chronos, ChronosBolt, YingLong, VisionTS, Toto-Base and Sundial-Base trend downward. The red Kairos series sits lowest and furthest left. A dashed arrow labeled '5.6x smaller' points at it. Panel (b) is a horizontal bar chart of mean information density with error bars for datasets from Pure Sine Wave to Saugeen (W). Panel (c) is a column of colored example time series, from smooth to noisy. Panel (d) compares three tokenization schemes: point, fixed patch, and Mixture-of-Size, shown as colored dots grouped into boxes. Each scheme feeds a model-name box, and a vertical axis runs from small to large information density.
caption: (a) Comparison on the GIFT-Eval benchmark [3] demonstrates that our KAIROS achieves superior zero-shot forecasting performance (lower normalized MASE) while requiring significantly fewer parameters than existing TSFMs. (b) (c) Significant variation exists in information density (i.e., signal complexity) across and within different time series datasets. (d) Existing TSFMs primarily use tokenization methods like point-wise or fixed-size patching, while our KAIROS uses Mixture-of-Size Tokenization to dynamically adapt to information density, enabling the learning of generalizable rules rather than memorization.
abstract: Inherent temporal heterogeneity, such as varying sampling densities and periodic structures, has posed substantial challenges in zero-shot generalization for Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs). Existing TSFMs predominantly rely on massive parameterization to absorb such heterogeneity, as their static tokenization and positional encoding schemes entangle diverse temporal patterns into a fixed representation space, encouraging memorization rather than adaptation. To address this limitation, we propose Kairos, a flexible and parameter-efficient TSFM dedicated to forecasting tasks, which decouples temporal heterogeneity from model capacity through a novel tokenization perspective. Kairos introduces a dynamic patching tokenizer and a mixture-of-size encoding that adapt observational granularity to local information density, enabling fine-grained temporal abstraction without increasing model width or depth. In addition, we design a multi-granularity positional embedding based on dynamic rotary encodings, which conditions on instance-level spectral features and temporal structure induced by dynamic patching tokenization, allowing robust modeling of diverse temporal dependencies. Trained on a novel Predictability-Stratified Time-Series (PreSTS) corpus, Kairos achieves superior zero-shot performance with substantially fewer parameters on two mainstream benchmarks, GIFT-Eval and Time-Series-Library. The project page is at https://foundation-model-research.github.io/Kairos .
